newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Austria's Raiffeisen plans to expand in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Raiffeisen plans to expand in Hungary.

text.p: Austria's Raiffeisen Zentralbank AG said on Monday that it planned substantial expansion in Hungary, either by buying Mezobank Rt or increasing the number of the branches of Raiffeisen's banking unit in the country.

Peter Felcsuti, CEO of the subsidiary, Unicbank Rt, which is Hungary's ninth largest commercial bank by assets despite a relatively small network of nine branches, announced that the bank would change its name to Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt next year.

The reason for the change was that Raiffeisen, which had been a founder of Unicbank ten years ago, had boosted its stake to above 95 percent and that Unicbank was preparing for expansion, Felcsuti said.
"Those banks which want to stay on the increasingly competitive Hungarian market, must consider expansion," he told a news conference. "We plan expansion."

He said that Mezobank, which led tens of thousands of personal accounts, was made attractive for Raiffeisen, which had an expansion strategy for the whole Central Europe, by its large network and retail banking business.
Mezobank was much stronger in retail banking than Unicbank which had built up significant and lucrative positions in the entrepreneurial sector, Felcsuti said.
Hungary plans to privatise Mezobank next year.

Felcsuti said Unicbank would decide on bidding for Mezobank pending that the state allowed it to do a due diligence at the bank, and in that case it was likely to compete for Mezobank with Hungary's Postabank and several other investors.

He added that the successful privatisation of Magyar Hitel Bank Rt (MHB), which was sold to the Dutch ABN AMRO last week, made Mezobank, and also other state-owned banks which are still ahead of privatisation, more attractive.
Felcsuti said the purchase of Mezobank was not a necessary condition of Unicbank's expansion for which the bank had sufficient resources.
He added that Unicbank would increase shareholders' capital to around 15.7 billion forints this year from one billion in 1987, though it paid a dividend every year. @

The after-tax profit also increased every year and would probably reach six billion forints in 1996, compared with 4.82 billion in 1995, and this was likely to keep Unicbank as the most profitable bank relative to assets in Hungary, he said.
Unicbank sees its balance sheet total rising to 100 billion forints at the end of this year and between 125 and 130 billion next year, from 77 billion forints in 1995, Felcsuti said.

He added that the bank's position could substantially improve next year if the government could agree with foreign investors in the energy sector, in which Unicbank was strong, about the rate of an energy price rise due on January 1. @
The investors, which bought energy companies in 1995, plan billions of dollars of further investments in Hungary pending on an acceptable decision on the energy price rise.

If the investments start next year this would substantially strengthen demand for financing on the Hungarian market, where competition was sharp due to an oversupply of credits and low economic activity, Felcsuti said.
